subject: Serving churn observed in dedicated pool — customer summary & next steps
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@novacart.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: ops@novacart.com
Date: 2029-05-17T21:12:34Z
Subject: Sudden 503/timeout spike from our Dedicated pool (us-west)

Kimberly —

We're seeing a sharp increase in 503s and timeouts for many of our endpoints backed by the dedicated GPU pool (us-west). The first spike started ~2029-05-17T20:52Z and recurred in two waves; our internal retries are making it worse for some routes. Latency jumps from ~120ms to sustained 2-3s, and a small subset of requests are failing with 503.

Attached a small logs snippet and a metrics sparkline. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side (autoscaler, warm pools, routing)? This is impacting a subset of customers in our checkout flow.

Thanks —
Lina
Lina Park
Sr. SRE, NovaCart

Attachments:
- server-logs-snippet.txt (text)
- metrics-sparkline.png (image)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@novacart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-17T21:25:10Z
Subject: Re: Sudden 503/timeout spike from our Dedicated pool (us-west)

Hi Lina —

Thanks for the quick signal and the attachments. We're looking into this right now; I’ve opened JIRA INF-9342 and escalated to infra. Initial triage shows a correlation with several dedicated nodes entering warmup simultaneously, which caused transient KV-cache misses and a short autoscaler oscillation.

Immediate actions taken (currently):
- Rolled back the last autoscaler config change for the us-west dedicated cluster.
- Temporarily increased the warm pool by 20% for NovaCart tenancy.
- Enabled a targeted routing bypass for requests that hit fallback paths.

I’ll follow up with a timeline and a proposed post-incident summary once we have the full logs. Can we set a 30-minute bridge to sync at 22:00 UTC?

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll get you a clear timeline and remediation plan.

– Kimberly
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2029-05-17T22:05:45Z
Subject: FW: Sudden 503/timeout spike — initial RCA notes

Team — quick tech notes to include in the post-incident draft: 

Observed behavior:
- ~20:52Z and again ~21:10Z we see a cluster-wide churn where ~15% of NovaCart's dedicated nodes moved from idle->warmup simultaneously.
- During warmup, KV cache misses increased ~6x, triggering elevated tokenization latency and head-of-line blocking for smaller batch windows. Autoscaler interpreted the latency increase as load and attempted to spin additional nodes, creating brief capacity oscillation.

Root-cause hypothesis (preliminary):
1) Cron job for log rotation (customer-side) aligned with a periodic warmup policy on our end, causing a synchronized traffic pattern.
2) An autoscaler threshold tweak deployed last week reduced the damping interval; this made the autoscaler respond faster but less stably to transient warmups.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Reverted autoscaler threshold change (rolled back 2029-05-14 patch).
- Increased per-tenant warm pool for NovaCart + enabled warm-prefetch for hot prefixes.
- Added a short-term request hedging rule to reduce head-of-line effects.

Questions for postmortem and customer ask:
- Confirm exact impacted window for billing/credit (we should propose a customer goodwill credit).
- Do we need a long-term autoscaler damping improvement + a warmup jitter mechanism?

I'll draft the technical section and share for review.

— Ben
VP, Platform Operations

Date: 2029-05-18T09:15:00Z
Subject: Post-incident summary: dedicated-serving churn (us-west) — NovaCart impact and next steps

Hi Lina —

Thanks again for flagging this. Below is a concise summary of what happened, what we did, and our proposed next steps. We’ll host a longer postmortem doc in the shared Drive for any technical follow-ups.

1) What happened (brief timeline)
- 2029-05-17T20:52Z: First observed latency spike and 503s for NovaCart routes.
- 2029-05-17T20:52Z–21:20Z: Two waves of elevated errors (peak at ~21:05Z).
- 2029-05-17T21:00Z: Immediate mitigations applied (autoscaler rollback, warm pool increase).
- 2029-05-17T22:30Z: Error rates returned to baseline and additional stabilizers remained in place.

2) Root cause (summary)
- A confluence of synchronized warmups and a recently tightened autoscaler damping threshold led to transient capacity oscillation and KV-cache pressure, which produced higher latencies and some 503s.

3) Customer impact and scope
- Impacted services: checkout and inventory routing for a portion of traffic in us-west.
- Estimated affected window: 2029-05-17T20:52Z to 2029-05-17T22:30Z.
- Estimated percentage of requests affected for NovaCart: ~8–12% of traffic during the window.

4) Remediations and compensations
- Short-term fixes implemented: autoscaler rollback; warm-pool + prefetch; hedging rule.
- Long-term changes planned: implement autoscaler damping improvements, add warmup jitter, and add early-detection alerts for synchronous warmups.
- We propose a one-time invoice credit equal to 25% of usage billed for the impacted window as a goodwill gesture.

5) Next steps / asks from NovaCart
- Please confirm the exact scope you see on your side (we have attached server-logs-snippet.txt and a metrics sparkline).
- If acceptable, we'll schedule a technical follow-up next week to walk through the proposed long-term fixes and timeline.

Attached: redwood-postmortem-draft.pdf (technical sketch), server-logs-snippet.txt, metrics-sparkline.png

Meeting links / evidence:
- Postmortem doc (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1NovaCartIncident-evidence
- Incident ticket: JIRA INF-9342

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll own the fix and communicate progress.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Infra Reliability — Redwood Inference
